The paper derives ATE minimax lower bounds in pure and smoothness-augmented structure-agnostic classes and proposes doubly robust asymptotically linear inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 52(2), 2024, version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives minimax CATE rates in a Hölder-smooth model and supplies a local-polynomial estimator, rather than a global ATE public-function weak-overlap frontier.
The paper links arbitrarily large inverse weights to irregular identification and tail-dependent slower-than-parametric rates, including an exogenous-selection treatment-effect example.
The paper studies robust confidence intervals for ATEs under limited overlap; it does not state the proposed four-channel public-function honest-length minimax result.
The general structure-agnostic ATE theory assumes bounded-away-from-zero overlap in its ATE treatment and explicitly lists weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: State an explicit validation-data or observable-certification regime for the adaptive OEQ, clarifying which quantities can certify each global L2 radius without oracle access.
Extend the converse from reservoir-rich constants to a necessary-and-sufficient shell-geometry condition, thereby determining whether individual channels vanish on tight shell classes.
Add a direct corollary contrasting the theorem’s required non-uniform overlap with the uniform-overlap assumptions in JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0; retain the accepted reservoir-rich-shell scope and preserve the adaptive problem as an explicit sequel.
